title: Cap. X: Habitual aversion / third ration — infants without peccasse-cum-Adamo
pass_a_gloss: Second (Placeus recites the reasons as they stand in D. Garissoles): habitual aversion cannot even be understood unless actual aversion has preceded. That is strikingly false if the actual aversion meant is the infants' own. Otherwise who denies that Adam's actual aversion preceded the habitual one in him, and that this was propagated into the little ones? Indeed aversion from God, in whomever it is, is sin by the very fact that it is aversion from God. Third: imagine some infant has aversion and reatus and yet did not sin with Adam — who can grasp that he is deservedly rebuked and ought to be punished? What fault has he in that he was so generated? Could he prevent being so begotten?
pass_b_english: Second — I recite the reasons as they stand in D. Garissoles — habitual aversion cannot even be conceived unless actual aversion went before. That is strikingly false if the actual aversion meant is the infants' own. Who denies that Adam's own actual turning from God preceded the habitual turn in him, and that this was passed down into the little ones? Aversion from God, wherever it is found, is sin simply because it is aversion from God. Third: imagine an infant who has aversion and guilt yet never sinned with Adam — how is he justly blamed and punished? What is his fault in being born so? Could he stop being begotten that way?
source_text: Secundo (recito enim has rationes ut apud D. Garissolium extant) aversio habitualis, nisi praecesserit actualis, ne intelligi quidem potest. Hoc vero insigniter falsum est, si actualis aversio ipsorum parvulorum intelligitur. Alioqui quis negat aversionem actualem Adami praecessisse habitualem in ipso, & hanc esse in parvulos propagatam? Profecto aversio a Deo, in quocunque sit, hoc ipso quod est aversio a Deo, peccatum est. Tertio, fingamus parvulum aliquem habere aversionem & reatum, & tamen non peccasse cum Adamo, quis capere poterit, eum merito reprehendi, & puniri debere. Quam culpam habet in eo, quod ita generatus est? Num impedire potuit, ne sic gigneretur?

choices.decision: Adam's actual aversion preceded and was propagated; aversion from God is sin wherever found

notes: Cap. X Theologorum auxilium densify section 121 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 124–127 tip).
